notes: Called or invited, often with the sense of being summoned by God. Paul is "called to be an apostle" (1:1), and the Roman believers are "called to be saints" (1:7). The related verb kaleō is the word for "to call."

elsewhere.note: Many are called, but few are chosen.
Called to be saints.
To those who are called.
Called and chosen and faithful.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Anger, especially God's settled opposition to evil, and the judgment that follows. In Romans, "the wrath of God is revealed from heaven" (1:18), and Paul says it is stored up for the day of judgment (2:5, 2:8). It is not a loss of temper but God's response to injustice.

elsewhere.note: Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
By nature children of wrath.
Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To uncover, to reveal what was hidden. In Romans, God's righteousness is "revealed" in the gospel (1:17), and his wrath is "revealed" against ungodliness (1:18). The related noun apokalypsis gives us the Greek name of the book of Revelation.

elsewhere.note: You have hidden these things from the wise and revealed them to little children.
So that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
God has revealed to us through the Spirit.
The faith that was to be revealed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To judge, to decide, to separate. Paul warns the person who "judges" others and does the same (2:1-3), and says God will judge people's secrets by Christ Jesus (2:16). The word is behind "critic," "criterion," and "crisis."

elsewhere.note: Judge not, that you be not judged.
God did not send his Son to condemn the world.
Do not pronounce judgment before the time.
They will give account to him who is ready to judge.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Kindness, goodness, benevolence. Paul says that God's "goodness" is meant to lead people to repentance (2:4). It is one of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22) and is used of God's kindness in Titus 3:4.

elsewhere.note: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness.
The immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us.
Put on compassionate hearts, kindness.
When the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Law, in Paul usually the Law of Moses (the Torah), though sometimes a principle ("the law of faith," 3:27; "the law of sin," 7:23). Romans uses the word about seventy-five times. Paul says the law shows sin, cannot make anyone righteous, and yet is "holy and righteous and good" (7:12). What he means in each use is a matter of discussion.

elsewhere.note: I have not come to abolish the Law but to fulfill it.
The law was given through Moses.
The law was our guardian until Christ came.
Whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A word used in the Greek Old Testament for the "mercy seat," the lid of the ark where atonement was made (Leviticus 16). Paul says God "put forward" Jesus as a hilastērion (3:25). Translators render it "atoning sacrifice," "propitiation" (turning aside wrath), "expiation" (removing sin), or "mercy seat."

range.note: A sacrifice that turns away wrath.

elsewhere.note: Above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat.

uncertain: Whether hilastērion in Romans 3:25 means a propitiation, an expiation, or the mercy seat is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to reckon, to count, to credit
notes: A bookkeeping word: to count, calculate, or credit to an account. Paul uses it about eleven times in Romans 3 and 4: Abraham's faith "was accounted to him for righteousness" (4:3), and "the Lord will not count" sin against the one he forgives (4:8). It is the word used in Genesis 15:6 in the Greek Old Testament.

elsewhere.note: He was counted among the lawless.
He was numbered with the transgressors.
Not counting their trespasses against them.
It was counted to him as righteousness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A promise, especially God's promise. For Paul the main one is the promise to Abraham, that he would be the father of many nations and heir of the world (4:13-21), which does not depend on law but on faith. The same word names the promised Holy Spirit in Acts 2:33.

elsewhere.note: I am sending the promise of my Father upon you.
He has received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit.
The promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring.
Imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be fully convinced, to fulfill
notes: To bring to full measure, to fully convince, or to fulfill completely. Abraham was "fully assured" that God could do what he promised (4:21). Paul uses the same word about each person being "fully convinced" in their own mind (14:5).

elsewhere.note: The things that have been accomplished among us.
Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
Fulfill your ministry.
Through me the message might be fully proclaimed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The act of declaring someone righteous, acquittal. Paul says Jesus "was raised for our justification" (4:25). It appears only here and in 5:18 in the New Testament.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: "Good news," the gospel. Paul is "set apart for the gospel of God" (1:1) and "not ashamed of the gospel" (1:16).

range.note: News of a king's triumph or accession.
The message about Jesus, later also a name for books like Mark.

elsewhere.note: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The gospel I preached to you.
The gospel that was preached by me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Righteousness, being in the right. Romans is about "the righteousness of God" (1:17, 3:21-22), and how people are counted righteous.

range.note: Living in line with God's will.
Fairness and rightness in dealings with others.
Being declared in the right before God (especially in Paul).

elsewhere.note: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.
That in him we might become the righteousness of God.
The righteousness from God that depends on faith.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To set apart, to separate for a purpose. Paul is "set apart for the gospel of God" (1:1).

elsewhere.note: Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul.
Who set me apart before I was born.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To hand over. "God gave them up" three times in 1:24, 1:26, 1:28, and Jesus "was delivered up for our trespasses" (4:25).

range.note: Pass something on, as a teaching.

elsewhere.note: Judas: "What will you give me?"
God did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all.
The night in which he was betrayed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Trust, faithfulness, and belief. It is the central word of Romans, occurring about forty times.

range.note: Confidence in a person or what they can do.
Being trustworthy and loyal (STEPBible tags this sense separately).

elsewhere.note: Your faith has made you well.
By grace you have been saved through faith.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A change of mind that leads to a change of life. God's goodness "leads you to repentance" (2:4).

elsewhere.note: Produce fruit worthy of repentance.
Repentance toward God.
Godly sorrow produces repentance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Conscience, moral awareness. Gentiles show the law "written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness" (2:15).

range.note: The inner sense of right and wrong.

elsewhere.note: I have lived before God in all good conscience.
Their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
From a pure heart and a good conscience.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Circumcision, the sign of the covenant with Abraham. Paul says real circumcision is "of the heart" (2:29), and that Abraham received it as a seal of faith he already had (4:11).

elsewhere.note: The circumcision party criticized Peter.
In Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts.
We are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To justify, to declare righteous. "By the works of the law, no flesh will be justified" (3:20), and "justified freely by his grace" (3:24).

elsewhere.note: This man went down to his house justified.
Not justified by works of the law.
Justified by his grace.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Redemption, release by payment. "Through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus" (3:24).

elsewhere.note: Your redemption is near.
In him we have redemption through his blood.
Redemption of the transgressions.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Favor, grace. "Justified freely by his grace" (3:24). Grace is the language of Romans from 1:5 to 16:20.

elsewhere.note: The Word was full of grace and truth.
The gospel of the grace of God.
By grace you are saved.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Splendor, honor, and the visible presence of God. "All have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God" (3:23).

elsewhere.note: They saw his glory.
The light of the knowledge of the glory of God.
He is the radiance of God's glory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sin, missing the mark. In Romans sin is almost a power, as in "under sin" (3:9); the word is used about forty-eight times.

range.note: A wrong against God or others.

elsewhere.note: He will save his people from their sins.
The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
If we confess our sins.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Exchange, and so the restoring of a broken relationship. Paul says that "while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son" (5:10-11). It is also used of the "reconciliation of the world" (11:15) and in 2 Corinthians 5:18-19, where Paul calls his work "the ministry of reconciliation."

range.note: A change from enmity to friendship.

elsewhere.note: He gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ.
If their rejection means the reconciliation of the world.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Steadfastness under pressure, literally "staying under." It is not passive: it is the stubborn endurance of a soldier or runner. Paul says "suffering produces perseverance" (5:3-4) and that we wait for what we hope for "with patience" (8:25).

elsewhere.note: They bear fruit with patience.
By your endurance you will gain your lives.
Through great endurance.
The testing of your faith produces steadfastness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Wages, especially a soldier's pay or rations. "The wages of sin is death" (6:23). Paul uses it in 1 Corinthians 9:7 and 2 Corinthians 11:8 for support given to workers. The contrast is with charisma, a free gift.

elsewhere.note: Be content with your wages.
Who serves as a soldier at his own expense?
I robbed other churches, accepting support from them.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to enslave, to make a slave
notes: To make someone a slave, or to bring under bondage. Paul says that believers were "freed from sin" and "enslaved to God" (6:18, 6:22). The verb makes the point that one is always owned by something; the question is by whom.

elsewhere.note: Not slaves to much wine.
I have made myself a servant to all.
We were enslaved to the elementary principles of the world.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Strong desire, whether good or bad, though in Paul it is usually a harmful craving. The tenth commandment, "you shall not covet" (7:7-8), uses the related verb. In the New Testament it often means the cravings of the flesh.

elsewhere.note: The desires for other things enter in.
I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you.
You will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
Not conforming to the passions of your former ignorance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Placing as a son, the legal adoption of a child as a full heir. Paul says believers "received the Spirit of adoption" (8:15) and that we wait "for adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies" (8:23). Adoption in Rome gave the adopted person full rights of inheritance, which is Paul's point.

range.note: Legal acceptance as a child and heir.

elsewhere.note: To them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants.
So that we might receive adoption as sons.
He predestined us for adoption as sons.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To know beforehand. Paul says "whom he foreknew, he also predestined" (8:29) and that God did not reject "his people whom he foreknew" (11:2). In the Bible knowing is relational as well as factual, so some read "foreknew" as "set his love on beforehand," others as God's advance knowledge.

elsewhere.note: They have known for a long time.
He was foreknown before the foundation of the world.

uncertain: What "foreknew" means in Romans 8:29 (advance knowledge or an act of choosing) is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To mark out in advance, to determine beforehand. In Romans 8:29-30, those whom God foreknew he "predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son." The word occurs in Acts 4:28, 1 Corinthians 2:7, and Ephesians 1:5 and 1:11. Debates about its meaning have shaped much Christian theology.

elsewhere.note: To do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place.
God decreed before the ages for our glory.
He predestined us for adoption.
Having been predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things.

uncertain: How to understand predestination in Romans 8 and 9, whether of individuals or of a people, is debated across Christian traditions.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A verdict of condemnation, and the punishment that follows. Paul says, "There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus" (8:1). It occurs only here, in 5:16, and in 5:18.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A groan or sigh of distress. In Romans 8:26 the Spirit intercedes "with groanings which can't be uttered." It appears elsewhere only in Acts 7:34, where God hears the groaning of Israel in Egypt.

elsewhere.note: I have heard their groaning.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Peace in the full sense of shalom. "We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" (5:1).

elsewhere.note: "Peace to you."
My peace I give to you.
The peace of God that surpasses understanding.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Hope, confident expectation. "Hope doesn't disappoint us" (5:5), and "in hope we were saved" (8:24).

elsewhere.note: The hope and resurrection of the dead.
Now faith, hope, and love abide.
A living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A slave or bondservant. "You are slaves of the one whom you obey" (6:16), and Paul says he is a bondservant of Christ (1:1).

range.note: A title of honor for those who serve the Lord.

elsewhere.note: Whoever wishes to be first among you must be your slave.
I would not be a servant of Christ.
Taking the form of a servant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Life, especially the life that comes from God. "The free gift of God is eternal life" (6:23), and the Spirit "of life" (8:2).

range.note: Life of the age to come.

elsewhere.note: That they may have life, and have it abundantly.
The free gift of God is eternal life.
Whoever has the Son has life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: eternal, of the age to come
notes: Eternal, of the age to come. "Eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (6:23).
uncertain: How to understand "eternal punishment" (25:46), as endless or as belonging to the age to come, has been debated across church history.

elsewhere.note: What good thing shall I do to have eternal life?
That whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
God gave us eternal life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Flesh, the physical body, and for Paul human nature under sin's power. "Those who walk according to the flesh" are set against "those who walk according to the Spirit" (8:4-13).

elsewhere.note: The Word became flesh.
The desires of the flesh are against the Spirit.
Jesus Christ has come in the flesh.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Breath, wind, or spirit. In Romans 8 it is the Holy Spirit, who lives in believers, leads them, and prays for them.

range.note: The Holy Spirit, or a spirit being.
Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
Receive the Holy Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The verb of self-giving love. "The love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord" (8:35-39) uses the related noun.

range.note: Care for another that shows itself in action.

elsewhere.note: Love your enemies.
Love one another as I have loved you.
We love because he first loved us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An Aramaic word for "father," warm and familiar. "By whom we cry, 'Abba! Father!'" (8:15), as Jesus cried in Gethsemane (Mark 14:36).

range.note: A child's and an adult's word for father.

elsewhere.note: Abba, Father, all things are possible to you.
The Spirit cries, "Abba! Father!"

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Religious service, worship, especially service rendered to God. It is used of Israel's temple service (9:4) and of the believer's whole life offered to God (12:1). The related verb latreuō is used of serving God.

elsewhere.note: Whoever kills you will think he is offering service to God.
Regulations for worship.
The priests go regularly into the first section, performing their ritual duties.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A choosing out, a selection. In Romans 9 to 11 it refers to God's choice of Israel and of a remnant (9:11, 11:5, 11:7, 11:28). Paul also speaks of Saul as God's "chosen instrument" (Acts 9:15). How election works is one of the great debates of theology.

elsewhere.note: He is a chosen instrument of mine.
Knowing your election.
Make your calling and election sure.

uncertain: Whether election in Romans 9 to 11 concerns individuals' destinies, the choice of a people for a purpose, or both, is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: What is left over, a remnant. Paul says "there is a remnant according to the election of grace" (11:5), in the line of the seven thousand left in Elijah's day. It occurs only here in the New Testament.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: That which fills or completes: fullness, full number, fulfillment. Paul speaks of Israel's "fullness" (11:12), "the fullness of the Gentiles" (11:25), and love as "the fulfillment of the law" (13:10). It is an important word also in Colossians and Ephesians.

elsewhere.note: The patch tears away from the garment.
They took up twelve baskets full.
From his fullness we have all received.
When the fullness of time had come.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To graft a branch into a tree. Paul says wild olive branches are "grafted in" among the natural branches (11:17, 11:19, 11:23-24), and that broken branches can be grafted in again. It occurs only in this chapter in the New Testament.

range.note: Join a branch to a tree.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Literally "to say the same," to agree, acknowledge, or publicly declare. Paul says that if you "confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord" and believe in your heart, you will be saved (10:9-10). It is the verb of the earliest Christian creeds.

elsewhere.note: Whoever acknowledges me before men.
He confessed, and did not deny.
You made the good confession.
Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To announce like a herald (kēryx), to proclaim publicly. Paul says "How will they hear without a preacher?" (10:14-15). The noun kērygma means the message proclaimed.

elsewhere.note: From that time Jesus began to preach.
Jesus came proclaiming the gospel of God.
Philip proclaimed to them the Christ.
We preach Christ crucified.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A spoken word, a saying. Paul says, "The word (rhēma) is near you," quoting Deuteronomy 30:14, and "Faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word (rhēma) of Christ" (10:8, 10:17). It differs from logos in stressing what is actually said.

elsewhere.note: Man shall live by every word that comes from the mouth of God.
Nothing will be impossible with God.
The sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
Upholds the universe by the word of his power.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Intense passion, in a good sense zeal and in a bad sense jealousy or envy. Paul says Israel has "a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge" (10:2). He also speaks of provoking Israel to "jealousy" (10:19, 11:11, 11:14).

elsewhere.note: Zeal for your house will consume me.
Filled with jealousy.
Your zeal for me.
As to zeal, a persecutor of the church.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: From logos ("reason, word"): rational, reasonable, or spiritual. Paul calls the offering of the body "your spiritual service" or "reasonable service" (12:1). It occurs only here and in 1 Peter 2:2, "the pure spiritual milk."

elsewhere.note: Like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk.

uncertain: Whether logikē latreia in Romans 12:1 means "spiritual worship," "reasonable service," or "rational worship" is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The mind, the thinking and willing self. Paul says to be "transformed by the renewing of your mind" (12:2). He also speaks of a "debased mind" (1:28) and the "mind of the Lord" (11:34).

elsewhere.note: He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
We have the mind of Christ.
Be renewed in the spirit of your minds.
The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Self-giving love, the main word for love in the New Testament. Paul says "Let love be without hypocrisy" (12:9) and "Love does no wrong to a neighbor" (13:10). The related verb is agapaō.

elsewhere.note: As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you.
Faith, hope, and love abide, but the greatest of these is love.
The fruit of the Spirit is love.
God is love.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Love of strangers, hospitality. Paul says believers should be "given to hospitality" (12:13). The only other New Testament use is in Hebrews 13:2: "Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers."

elsewhere.note: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To show mercy. "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy" (9:15), and God "shut up all to disobedience that he might have mercy on all" (11:32).

elsewhere.note: Have mercy on us, Son of David.
Master, have mercy on us.
Have mercy on those who doubt.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A stumbling block, something that trips people. Paul quotes Isaiah about "a stumbling stone and a rock of offense" (9:32-33), and warns against putting a stumbling block before a brother (14:13).

range.note: The part of a trap that snaps shut.
Something that makes a person fall.

elsewhere.note: You are a hindrance to me.
A stumbling block to Jews.
The offense of the cross.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: End, goal, completion. "Christ is the end of the law" (10:4), in the sense of its goal, its termination, or both.

elsewhere.note: The one who endures to the end will be saved.
Then comes the end.
If we hold our confidence firm to the end.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To call on, to appeal. "Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved" (10:13).

elsewhere.note: Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
Those who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To announce good news. "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace" (10:15).

elsewhere.note: The poor have good news preached to them.
Philip tells him the good news about Jesus.
The good news was preached to us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to save, to heal, to make well
notes: To save, heal, or make well. "You will be saved" (10:9), "Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved" (10:13).

range.note: To save from danger or death.
To save in the fullest sense.

elsewhere.note: He will save his people from their sins.
Everyone who calls will be saved.
By grace you are saved.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A mystery, a secret that has been revealed. Paul says, "I don't desire, brothers, to have you ignorant of this mystery" (11:25).

range.note: Something hidden until it is disclosed.
In wider Greek, the secret rites of a cult.

elsewhere.note: The secrets of the kingdom of heaven.
Behold, I tell you a mystery.
The mystery was made known to me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To change form. "Be transformed by the renewing of your mind" (12:2). Jesus was "transfigured" with the same word.

elsewhere.note: He was transfigured before them.
Being transformed into the same image.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To conquer, to overcome. "Don't be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good" (12:21).

elsewhere.note: A stronger one attacks and overcomes him.
This is the victory that has overcome the world, our faith.
The one who conquers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To put or arrange under, to be in subjection voluntarily. Paul says "let every soul be in subjection to the higher authorities" (13:1, 13:5). It is a military word for rank, and is used in the New Testament of wives, slaves, citizens, and the whole church, with a sense of orderly relationship, not obedience in every case.

range.note: Take one's place in an order.

elsewhere.note: Whoever would be great among you must be your servant.
